tickets.narration_anchor: A guest finds the property, has a beautiful stay, and the operator later reviews the journey.
tickets.required_semantic_content: One specific modest independent inn, one recurring capable operator, one recurring guest, and a physical key-tag handoff that establishes a completed stay without implying consent.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a high-contrast neutral slate labeled TICKET: INN REALITY with the story job and no attractive proxy image.

tickets.narration_anchor: The OTA brings useful discovery, comparison, translated listings, paid marketing, and checkout reach.
tickets.required_semantic_content: Accurate permissioned material showing an OTA as a useful discovery and booking surface without recreating a branded interface, logo, price, or claim in the renderer.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a neutral slate labeled TICKET: OTA MARKET FORCE beside the useful OTA gate; never draw a fake platform screen.

tickets.narration_anchor: Cloudbeds looked at roughly ninety million bookings and found more than sixty percent came through OTAs.
tickets.required_semantic_content: A canonical capture of the exact vendor-published source context with publisher, page title, access date, highlighted claim, caveat, and enough surrounding text to avoid misleading extraction.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show an unmistakable neutral proof-ticket slate pinned to the affected nodes; do not synthesize source text or figures.

tickets.narration_anchor: The hotel pays for demand through commission and should put a real dollar figure next to the problem.
tickets.required_semantic_content: A redacted operator-side settlement statement or commission ledger that can demonstrate economic consequence without exposing guest data or using a guest-facing booking receipt as commission proof.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a neutral ledger-shaped slate marked OPERATOR PROOF REQUIRED with no invented line items, amounts, brand marks, or guest details.

tickets.narration_anchor: Mews raised a large funding round at a reported valuation, showing that hospitality software investment is not the missing ingredient by itself.
tickets.required_semantic_content: A canonical source capture for the exact Mews funding and valuation statement, including publisher, publication date, currency, surrounding context, and an explicit limitation that funding does not prove operating outcomes.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a conspicuous neutral slate labeled TICKET: MEWS SOURCE; display no invented headline, valuation, interface, logo, or source text.

tickets.narration_anchor: The reviewed providers did not publish one simple per-property price that could honestly be presented as a market rate.
tickets.required_semantic_content: A dated, reproducible review packet identifying the exact provider pages checked, the scope of the search, and the bounded conclusion that no simple public per-property price was located during that review.
rights_requirements: provider marks used only for source context
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a neutral EVIDENCE GAP ticket with the review scope and date fields blank; never infer a price or fabricate a provider comparison.

tickets.narration_anchor: The revenue-management salary range is labor-value evidence, not a per-hotel service price or revenue promise.
tickets.required_semantic_content: A canonical capture of the exact salary source with geography, role definition, date, range, unit, and the editorial limitation that it supports labor value only.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a neutral LABOR SOURCE REQUIRED slate with a visible NOT CLIENT PRICE limitation; do not invent salary text, charts, or source styling.

tickets.narration_anchor: Search on a phone, compare the direct rate, try to book, read the terms, and call when the desk is busy.
tickets.required_semantic_content: An original, authorized process capture of a real property's mobile direct path and call handoff, with current terms and property identity reviewed before use.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a neutral phone-outline slate labeled TICKET: DIRECT-PATH TEST; do not draw or infer an interface from narration.

tickets.narration_anchor: With the guest's permission, save enough information to make the next message useful.
tickets.required_semantic_content: A privacy-safe, authorized physical or procedural handoff that clearly distinguishes requesting permission, affirmative consent, revocation, suppression, and the later minimal context record.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a neutral gate slate labeled AFFIRMATIVE PERMISSION REQUIRED; never use a decorative contact-card stand-in.

tickets.narration_anchor: You approve the voice and offers, review anything sensitive, and decide when not to send.
tickets.required_semantic_content: An authorized operator review moment showing approve, reject, suppress, or escalate as real decisions without depicting generated copy, fake guest data, or a fake software interface.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a neutral HUMAN REVIEW ticket attached to the mandatory gate, with approve, suppress, and escalate as plain text labels only.

tickets.narration_anchor: The next booking takes the direct path and the hotel turns the introduction into a relationship it can keep.
tickets.required_semantic_content: An authorized, privacy-safe direct booking confirmation from the property that proves only the outcome and stays visually separate from settlement or commission evidence.
tickets.placeholder_behavior: Show a neutral outcome slate labeled DIRECT CONFIRMATION REQUIRED; never invent booking text, price, platform UI, or guest identity.
